parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The most common oxidation states of cobalt are +2 and +3.

Complete the electronic configurations of the following free ions.

• $\text{Co}^{2+}$ [Ar]

• $\text{Co}^{3+}$ [Ar]

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
$\text{Co}^{2+}$ and $\text{Co}^{3+}$ both form complexes with $\text{edta}^{4-}$.

| half-equation | $E^\ominus/\text{V}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{Co}^{3+} + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Co}^{2+}$ | +1.82 |
| $\text{O}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 4\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ | +1.23 |
| $[\text{Co}(\text{edta})]^- + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons [\text{Co}(\text{edta})]^{2-}$ | +0.38 |
| $\text{Co}^{2+} + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Co}$ | -0.28 |

Use the data in the table to predict what happens, if anything, when separate aqueous solutions of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ and $[\text{Co}(\text{edta})]^-$ are left to stand in the air.

aqueous solution of $\text{Co}^{3+}$

aqueous solution of $[\text{Co}(\text{edta})]^-$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Hydrated cobalt(II) nitrate, $\text{Co}(\text{NO}_3)_2\cdot6\text{H}_2\text{O}$, is a red solid that behaves like hydrated magnesium nitrate, $\text{Mg}(\text{NO}_3)_2\cdot6\text{H}_2\text{O}$, when heated.

Describe in detail what you would expect to observe when crystals of $\text{Co}(\text{NO}_3)_2\cdot6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ are heated in a boiling tube, gently at first and then more strongly.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why the thermal stability of the Group 2 nitrates increases down the group.
